audit.whatIsWrong: The chart (Skill/Singed/Singed/Skill/Skill/Singed/Singed) contradicted the prose on the same page, which says 'Yasuo owns levels 1-2 cleanly' and 'respect his 2-item spike hard'.
audit.why: Yasuo has Steel Tempest on a flat 4s and Sweeping Blade through minions from level 2 while Singed has no Mega Adhesive until 3; at two items Infinity Edge plus a third crit item outpaces Insanity Potion's regen. The packet chart already reflects this.
audit.corrected: Yasuo / Yasuo / Skill / Singed / Singed / Singed / Yasuo.

audit.why: Spike timings were right — Yasuo lvl 1-2, Singed proxy at 4-5, Rylai's, Yasuo's 2-item crit window. Only the mechanism text inside them needed fixing, not the timings.
audit.corrected: Numbers added: Wind Wall 25/23/21/19/17s for 4s, Last Breath 70/50/30s, Steel Tempest 4s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Wind Wall interaction was stated backwards in two places. wants.foe[1] told the reader Yasuo blocks 'your Fling projectile' — Fling is a 125-range targeted ability, not a projectile, and no wall stops it. Meanwhile mid says 'Windwall cannot block Poison Trail or Mega Adhesive' — Poison Trail is right, Mega Adhesive is not: it is a thrown vial and Singed's own kit file flags it projectile, 'can be blocked by Wind Wall-class effects'. Also missing entirely: Mega Adhesive grounds, and grounding turns Sweeping Blade off completely — the single most important thing Singed does to Yasuo.
audit.why: This is the Azir/Wind Wall failure exactly. A player told the wall eats Fling will not throw Fling; a player told the wall cannot eat Mega Adhesive will throw the goo straight into it and lose it for 17 seconds at rank 5. The grounding is what turns a mobile duelist into a walker.
audit.corrected: Poison Trail is an aura and passes through Wind Wall untouched. Mega Adhesive is a thrown projectile and the wall does block it — throw the goo before he draws the wall, or after its 4 seconds expire (25/23/21/19/17s). Fling is targeted at 125 range and nothing blocks it. Standing in Mega Adhesive, Yasuo is grounded: Sweeping Blade will not cast at all. Last Breath needs an Airborne enemy, so it is his own Steel Tempest whirlwind that sets it up, never your Fling.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flagged 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere', and worse, the full layer's tracked enemy ability was set to 'Yasuo Poison Trail' — Poison Trail is Singed's own Q. Every cooldown line, the do, the focus and the report row all told the reader to track Yasuo's Poison Trail.
audit.why: A tracked cooldown that belongs to the wrong champion is unusable. The ability that actually gates Singed's sequencing here is Wind Wall.
audit.corrected: Track Wind Wall: 4 seconds up, 25/23/21/19/17s down. Throw Mega Adhesive outside that window. Last Breath 70/50/30s is the second clock.

audit.whatIsWrong: Sweeping Blade was described as free repeatable mobility on you.
audit.why: It cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for several seconds. Against you specifically he gets one dash, then must use minions.
audit.corrected: Sweeping Blade re-targets in 0.5/0.4/0.3/0.2/0.1s but is locked out on the same enemy for a few seconds — after he E's through you, he needs a minion to keep moving. Deny minions and you deny the escape.

edits.before: Level 4 is where this lane pivots: start the proxy. Run your Poison Trail through the wave on the far side of his tower and force him to either recall, leave lane, or chase you into the cloud — none of those choices suit a duelist champion who needs to stack Steel Tempest on minions. At level 6, Insanity Potion makes the equation brutal for him: you gain enough armor, magic resist, and regeneration that standing in your poison hurts him far more than trading autos hurts you, and Windwall cannot block Poison Trail or Mega Adhesive. Drop the sticky goo at the edge of a wall or jungle entrance when he tries to dash out, root him in it, and Fling him back into the cloud — that is a kill pattern he has no clean answer for in this window.
edits.after: Level 4 is where this lane pivots: start the proxy. Run your Poison Trail through the wave on the far side of his tower and force him to either recall, leave lane, or chase you into the cloud — none of those choices suit a duelist who needs to stack Steel Tempest on minions. At level 6, Insanity Potion makes the equation brutal for him. Wind Wall cannot block Poison Trail, but it does eat the Mega Adhesive vial, so throw the goo before he draws the wall or after its 4 seconds run out. Land it on him and he is grounded — Sweeping Blade will not cast — then Fling him back into the cloud. A Fling into that glue roots him outright, and that is a kill pattern he has no clean answer for in this window.

edits.before: Rylai's makes your side-lane an absolute menace — every Poison Trail tick slows Yasuo as he tries to chase, and a slowed Yasuo cannot chain Sweeping Blade dashes freely enough to escape or all-in safely. Push that advantage by forcing 1-3-1 split pressure and making him follow you rather than grouping for his ideal Last Breath teamfight. However, respect his 2-item spike hard: Infinity Edge into a third crit item gives him the burst to Last Breath-combo you before Insanity Potion's regeneration ticks matter, especially if you are caught at less than half health. Do not face-check chokepoints where a Steel Tempest tornado can set up his ult remotely — keep Mega Adhesive in hand and run toward your own structures if he hard-commits.
edits.after: Rylai's makes your side-lane a menace — every Poison Trail tick slows Yasuo, and grounded in Mega Adhesive he cannot Sweeping Blade at all. Push that by forcing 1-3-1 split pressure and making him follow you rather than grouping for his ideal Last Breath teamfight. However, respect his 2-item spike hard: Infinity Edge into a third crit item gives him the burst to combo you before Insanity Potion's regeneration matters. Last Breath needs you Airborne, and only his own Steel Tempest whirlwind can do that — never face-check a chokepoint where that tornado reaches you first. Hold Mega Adhesive for his commit and run toward your own structures rather than trading in the open, and remember Way of the Wanderer rebuilds his shield the whole time he is walking at you.

notes: The full layer for this matchup had Singed's own Q filled in as the enemy ability to track — 'Yasuo Poison Trail' appeared in the tldr, winCon, dosFull[0], breakdown.cooldowns, focus and report[5]. I corrected all of those to Wind Wall except focus.text, which I left alone: focus.text still reads 'Yasuo Poison Trail' and focus.letters is ['Q']. Both should become Wind Wall / ['W'] but I did not want to edit focus without confirming the letters array maps to the enemy's slot rather than yours. Separately: yasuo.json's derived flags list Wind Wall as terrain that 'blocks paths and dashes'. Riot's own description says it blocks projectiles only, and per the standing rule I trusted the description — no dash-blocking claim was written. All 3 suspectNames are false positives.
